Grant him mercy and granted mercy differ materially, as do richly/so richly. The later official Talon line is era-specific Archmother material and remains separate.
Revision 2 is the complete grammatical line; revision 1 ends with a truncated mo- and cannot be a finished subtitle.
Them versus 'em is an audible elision and both complete phrases are grammatical.
Both revisions preserve the malformed take an escape phrase, and one also misspells Yamato; neither is clearly correct.
A condition can be a curse, and the contrast with learning to use it is coherent; occurs is a generated homophone error.
Let's get back and Let's go get back are both grammatical but differ by the audible verb go.
Cutting it a little close is the established idiom and is independently used in the parallel Abrams/Orion line; revision 0 omits it.
The see_money context makes I shouldn't leave that money behind the coherent pickup motivation; should reverses the intended action.
Revision 0 includes an audible Oh absent from revision 1; punctuation and hash count cannot resolve it.
A pity we won't be working together is the grammatical idiom; I pity requires an object.
You thought you'd be safe up there is the natural taunt after a mid-air kill; You've thought is an ill-fitting tense in this event context.
'em versus them is an audible elision and both forms are grammatical.
Will and would differ in audible modality and both can be intentional patron predictions.
Called on the patron and called upon the patrons differ in preposition and number; both are grammatical ritual language.
The game object is the Spirit Jar, while one revision says spirit urn and the other omits Jar; neither existing component revision is clearly correct, and prototype terminology may differ.
Revision 2 exactly uses established Spirit Jar terminology and forms a grammatical sentence; the other revisions are corrupt segmentations.
Both component revisions are corrupt variants of the coherent Justice line outside the component; game and case are not supported by narrative context.
Haze and OSIC are authoritative spellings, and the separate official line confirms the generated wording while its Hidden King invocation remains distinct.
Parallel male and Mirage alias lines identify the addressee as Sandeep/Mirage; Xandri and Sand Deep are both unsupported names.
They'd/They is an audible auxiliary difference, and colloquial They better is plausible speech.
